questions.q: What does an Azure Backup policy attached to a Recovery Services vault define?
options: How often backups run and how long each backup is retained
Only which Availability Zone a VM is deployed into
The network security group rules for a subnet
Only the maximum size of a single backup file
questions.explain: An Azure Backup policy configures both backup frequency and retention for the resources attached to the vault.

questions.q: What does an AWS Backup plan do differently from configuring EBS snapshot schedules resource-by-resource?
options: It centralizes backup rules and lifecycle across multiple resource types like EBS and RDS from one place
It can only be applied to a single EBS volume at a time
It replaces the need for any retention policy
It only works for resources outside of AWS
questions.explain: AWS Backup plans apply backup rules and lifecycle (retention) across supported resource types centrally, rather than configuring each resource individually.

questions.q: What question does a retention policy answer, separate from backup frequency?
options: How long a backup is kept before it's deleted
How many servers are included in the backup
What time zone the backup job runs in
Which cloud provider's backup service is faster
questions.explain: Frequency is how often backups run; retention is a separate decision about how long each resulting backup sticks around.

questions.q: Why is 'keep every backup forever' not considered a real retention policy in this lesson?
options: Storage cost grows without bound, and most old recovery points are never actually restored from
Cloud providers technically prohibit keeping backups past 30 days
Backups automatically corrupt after a year regardless of settings
It is actually the recommended approach for all resources
questions.explain: Unbounded retention means unbounded storage cost for recovery points that, realistically, are almost never used.

questions.q: What is the core idea behind tiered retention (e.g. daily for a week, weekly for a month, monthly for a year)?
options: Keep backups dense for recent history and progressively sparser further back, covering the same span at lower storage cost
Delete all backups older than 24 hours automatically
Only keep one single backup at any given time
Run backups more frequently as they get older
questions.explain: Tiered retention keeps fine-grained recovery points for the recent past and coarser ones further back, instead of storing full daily history indefinitely.
